appraisal_events.evidence: "Chaque fois je lui écrivis de n'en rien faire, en invoquant l'excuse d'être obligé de m'absenter..."; "Sans doute me jugea-t-il mal en apprenant par sa tante en quoi consistait le devoir de famille"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator repeatedly turns away Saint-Loup's offers to visit him at Balbec, inventing a family-duty pretext to protect his time with the petite bande; on learning the truth, Robert probably judges him poorly, though this is narrated with hedging ('sans doute') rather than asserted as certain.

status_effects.explanation: He repeatedly seeks out the narrator's company and is turned away each time under a fabricated pretext.
Robert is said to probably think less of him once he learns the real, trivial-seeming reason for the repeated refusals.

ambiguities: Robert's negative judgment of the narrator is presented with explicit narratorial hedging ('sans doute me jugea-t-il mal') rather than as a certain, witnessed fact, which lowers confidence in this reading.
